Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Light Up a Life 2026

Hilary Gotts asked on here last week whether we are doing the tree again this year. Yes, Hilary, we are, and please do bring your sister.

The practical details first, as I know some of you like to get things in the diary.

Memory tags will be in the shop from Monday 16 November. The suggested donation is £3. There are envelopes on the counter if you would rather take a tag away and write it at home, which a good many people do.

We switch the lights on at 4pm on Saturday 28 November, here on Magdalen Street. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing three or four carols, and Doreen is making her mince pies again. Going by last year, I would get here before the first carol if you want one.

Every name on the tags will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You are very welcome to come, but you don't need to be there for your name to be read.

Now, if you'll allow me a few lines of my own. My husband Ray died at the hospice in November 2019, so it is seven years this month. The first year I hung his tag I could hardly write it. Now I write it at the counter, with the same pen. I mention it only because some of you will be writing a tag for the first time this year, and I remember what that first one is like. Take as long as you need over it, and take it home if that is easier.

There are two things I would like everybody to know.

The tree is for anyone who is grieving. The person you are remembering doesn't have to have been cared for by the hospice, and you don't have to have any connection with us at all. If you are missing somebody, it is your tree as much as mine.

You also don't have to buy anything, or write anything. If all you want is to come in out of the cold and stand by the tree for a few minutes, please do. Nobody will mind, and nobody will hurry you along. Some of the nicest moments in the shop last December were people doing exactly that, usually with a bag of shopping in each hand.

Lastly, thank you for last year. The tree carried 412 names by the time the lights went on, and I read a good many of them while I was hanging them up. I am told that between you, you kept the hospice's night sitters going for the best part of a month. I think of that sometimes when I am locking up in the dark.

So do come in from the 16th. We'll have the tags ready and the pen on the counter.

Jean
